en: The Text of the Bodhisattva Precepts, Volume One.
With a mind of cool serenity, I thirstily yearn for and concentrate upon the sound of the Dharma. I pray that the Precept Master will graciously expound it as extensively as a lake.
[The Master] says: "All Bodhisattvas must not kill living beings. To kill a living being is certain to lead to a fall into the great hells. To take life...
In future lives, one will receive the retribution of a short lifespan;
in this Sahā world, both eyes may be injured and one may become blind.
Therefore, I exhort all those in the place of practice to collectively sever the karma of killing and not commit it.
O Sons of the Buddha, let no Bodhisattva steal or take what belongs to another.
For instance, there was once a woman who died young and was immediately reborn as an animal with fur and horns to seek retribution.
She was driven and harnessed all day long, never finding rest.
Without any effort, they feed on water and grass;
yet their deluded minds remain unaware.
For this reason, I report this to you with earnestness and urgency.
O Son of the Buddha!
May all bodhisattvas refrain from sexual misconduct.
Sexual misconduct is a root of sin characterized by perversion; its retribution is the appearance of glowing iron beds, scorching and pressing together toward one.
The saws were blazing as they vied with one another to come; their bodies were completely covered, every part of them drenched.
He cried out, "Why do you not give rise to the bodhicitta?
O Son of the Buddha!"
"O Bodhisattvas, do not speak falsely.
Having come here, who would go away without seeing what they have seen?
Those who deceive with empty words shall have their tongues ploughed by iron plows."
Furthermore, one who understands how to release the saw shall see what is beneficial.
Or, if sentient beings deceive their teachers, monks, or parents,
if they can repent and do not remain resentful, they will surely be freed from the suffering of *pātaka* in the future.
O Sons of the Buddha,
let no bodhisattvas trade in wine;
those who do shall have molten copper poured into their mouths.
Fire erupts from beneath your feet, its flames reaching to the heavens;
the hell-wardens, wielding spears, sever both your hands—
all this is due solely to your delusion and inverted views.
The consequences of one's actions in a human body must be experienced by oneself;
one will still be driven and plundered into the Avīci hell,
where there are no places of refuge amidst its thousandfold layers of iron walls.
O Sons of the Buddha,
let the bodhisattvas not speak of themselves; let them instead speak through analogies,
like washing away the sins one has committed with hot water.
It is as if one were suddenly cast into a deep abyss and falls into a swoon;
from dawn until night, long nails are driven [into the body], and from the eyes and ears flow tears and blood.
This is the cause of sin, the fruit of sin, and the cooling of the root of sin.
Then ox-headed demons arrive to pull out their tongues, allowing them no chance to beg for their lives;
they are briefly released from the prison guards' grasp so that they may discharge [their filth].
O Son of the Buddha!
O Bodhisattvas, do not disparage others.
Those who disparage others will enter the hells;
they will be struck by swords and blades, subjected to forced labor, and driven across [the abyss].
Upon entering the mud and water of the hells, they become submerged and stupefied, as if in a boiling cauldron.
Having passed through all the hells,
their skin, flesh, and blood become like flowing water.
"When shall we be free from the *pāṭala*?
O Son of the Buddha,
may all bodhisattvas not be overly stingy."
He accumulated vast treasures;
yet when he saw a poor person coming to beg from his mountain retreat,
he could not restrain his greedy heart even for the sake of a single needle or a blade of grass.
Not knowing contentment,
one will enter the Yellow Springs empty-handed in the future.
O Son of the Buddha!
May all bodhisattvas not give rise to excessive anger;
those who harbor much anger will certainly undergo rebirth as a crawling snake,
writhing on its belly with no hands or feet.
Because of his anger in a previous life,
eighty thousand bamboo tubes have come to devour him,
leaving behind nothing but his own bones and skin.
The suffering experienced therein is unbearable.
O Son of the Buddha, when will one obtain a superior human body during this kalpa?
May all bodhisattvas not slander the Triple Gem.
Should they slander the Triple Gem, they shall fall into the evil realms;
three hundred conch-shell long nails shall be driven firmly into their bodies.
Cries of lamentation reach the heavens in a vast roar as they slander the Buddha;
their slandering grows even more intense, and as they give rise to anger, copper gates and iron bars come to crush them. How painful!
How bitter! It is beyond description. When will they encounter the hand of Heaven and find the Way?
O Son of the Buddha.
Huìyuán says:
From a single speck of dust up to the commission of the most extreme black offenses, one undergoes a thousand births.
The supreme fruit of Bodhi is thus entirely lost at once;
to dally with the six realms of existence is truly pitiable.
By what path can one take birth among the heavens and the human world?
The commentary says:
Having committed a violation of the precepts, one knows that retribution has already fallen into the three miserable realms;
as for how many years have passed while undergoing this state, it cannot yet be calculated.
The commentary says:
Having already fallen into the evil realms, one undergoes extreme suffering;
that this continues for further kalpas is truly lamentable.
In the course of years and months, one does not realize how long the mind has been in doubt as to whether it has already heard the names of the parents and the Triple Gem.
The Master said:
"Alas, alas! The Master said:
'Today I have heard the Lotus Treasury Precepts.'"
The assembly, with one mind, entreated him, saying, "We pray that you will deign to explain this extensively.
The Master replied,
"I now repent and dare not conceal anything."
"I only pray that the Preceptor will compassionately explain this in detail.
The Harmonizer replied,
"The Great Master’s secret treasury is the true exposition of the nectar of immortality."
"Rejoicing, I have now heard [this]; I pray that you will deign to explain it extensively.
The Master replied, "The Buddha-mind has been obstructed from being heard for kalpas of vast duration."
"Now that we have encountered this proclamation, we pray you will deign to explain it extensively.
The Master replied,
"The precepts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are rarely encountered in their proclamation."
I pray that the Preceptor of the Precepts will, out of compassion, explain this extensively. With a cooled heart and a sense of shame, I dare not conceal anything;
I lay bare my very heart and liver to confess and repent of the karmic obstacles of sins as numerous as the sands of the Ganges accumulated throughout vast kalpas.
Now, having heard these precepts, all [obstacles] are eliminated.
With shame and remorse, I offer this to the Preceptor with joyful devotion.
Recorded on the fourth day of the fourth month in the fourth year of the Qiánfú era, copied at Bào’ēn Monastery.
